claims.text: The high-temperature structural stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles is governed by atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion.
The high-temperature chemical stability of these nanoparticles is governed by atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion.
Precise control of synthesis parameters and subsequent thermal treatment can optimize atomic-scale ordering and lattice distortion.
The initial nanoparticles are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid solutions with an FCC crystal structure.
In situ TEM and XRD, combined with molecular dynamics simulations, can validate theoretical models and inform experimental design.
The proposed catalytic operating range is 773–1173 K.
The proposed thermoelectric operating range is 473–1923 K.
Testing will be conducted under inert Ar or N2 for up to 100 hours.
Optimizing composition, synthesis temperature, synthesis time, and thermal treatment produces a stable, ordered lattice.
A stable, ordered lattice increases resistance to degradation.
Increased resistance to degradation maintains catalytic and thermoelectric performance.
Optimized synthesis and thermal treatment will increase structural stability by 20% relative to conventionally synthesized, untreated nanoparticles.
Optimized synthesis and thermal treatment will improve chemical stability by 15% relative to conventionally synthesized, untreated nanoparticles.
TEM, XRD, and EDS can quantify the predicted structural and chemical stability changes.
The hypothesis applies from 773 to 1923 K.
The hypothesis applies when noble-metal content is below 10 at.%.
The hypothesis applies to nanoparticles 5–50 nm in size.

contradictions.description: The conditions include thermoelectric operation from 473 K, whereas the stated boundary limits the hypothesis to temperatures at or above 773 K.

The stated intervention is characterization and simulation rather than a controlled manipulation of ordering, lattice distortion, or thermal treatment, so it does not implement the intervention invoked by the hypothesis and mechanism.
